name: gusset_polygon_is_not_degenerate
why: ENTRY GP20, the second shape. The POLYGONAL profile is the one the library shipped up to 0.139.0, but with the two short sides at zero: a polygon that closes on itself, and SOLIDWORKS returns null with no reason given, even with mark 1 (measured on 28/9/2026, variants 0 and 3 of the probe Checks/Gusset/Program.cs). With real short sides (15 and 15) the same call IS BORN: +12937.5 mm3 (variant 2).
defect_caught: The degenerate polygon, that is exactly the old recipe: step 4 demands it refused BEFORE calling SOLIDWORKS, with a message that says «degenerate» and names the triangle. Step 5 takes the polygon with the short sides as long as the sides (60 out of 60): it is no longer a gusset, and that must be said instead of leaving it to SOLIDWORKS. Step 6 is the good polygon, with the measured numbers.
_and_the_twins_are_in_the_same_file: The good polygon (step 6) goes between the same two faces as the triangle of gusset_sits_in_the_corner. Step 4 removes only «side3_mm» and «side4_mm»; step 5 changes only «side3_mm» (60 instead of 15).
_the_selectors_are_measured: The same as in weld_bead_goes_between_touching_faces, measured on 25/9/2026 after the cut: between the two «front» faces of the long one of 40800 mm2 the outer one (z = 40) is the second, between the two «right» faces of the short one of 17680 the outer one (x = 340) is the first.
_the_expected_numbers: Computed by hand BEFORE, and compared with the probe. The polygon is the pentagon (0,0) (60,0) (60,15) (15,60) (0,60): the 60 x 60 square minus the 45 x 45 / 2 triangle that the tip loses, 3600 - 1012.5 = 2587.5 mm2, over 5 of thickness 12937.5 mm3 — the probe measured +12937.5. The part goes from 1264161.94 (the cut T, measured in the weld bead case) to 1277099.44. The box of the new body is computed by hand and NOT measured by the probe: the pentagon sits in the same 60 x 60 square as the triangle, so x from 340 to 400, y from -2.5 to 2.5, z from 40 to 100.

expect.tolerance_why: 40 mm x 1469.956 mm2 of section, which has pi inside (the corner radii). Without the cut the short one would stay inside the long one and there would be no common edge to rest the gusset on

(60 x 60 - 45 x 45 / 2) x 5, all flat and without chamfer: the probe of 28/9/2026 measured +12937.5 to the hundredth. A triangle in place of the polygon would give 9000, a polygon with the short sides read the wrong way round would give the same number (15 and 15), and that is why the box below

the cut T (1264161.94, measured in the weld bead case) plus the 12937.5 of the plate, read from the document and not from the answer of the operation; the half cubic millimetre is that of the weld bead case on the same part
read back from IGussetFeatureData.Thickness (metres): the thousandth is the rounding of the conversion to millimetres

the faces on which SOLIDWORKS says it rested the gusset (GetSupportingFaces), from the largest: 600 x 68 and 260 x 68; half a square millimetre out of tens of thousands is rounding, a wrong face is wrong by thousands

computed by hand (see «i_numeri_attesi»), read with the extreme points of the new body: all planar faces, so the extreme points are exact and the hundredth is the rounding to two decimals of the answer
